record.paper_title: Quantum Information Theory: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: What is a general formula for the capacity of an arbitrary quantum channel, that is, a formula that determines the ultimate asymptotic rate at which information can be transmitted reliably when the communication channel has genuinely quantum effects rather than being reducible to a classical channel or to a collection of special cases?

evidence.quote: This has not proven to be the case; even now, we do not have a general formula for the capacity of a quantum channel.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{N}: \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A) \to \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_B)$ be a quantum channel, i.e., a completely positive trace-preserving linear map between the bounded-operator algebras of finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. For each integer $n \geq 1$, an $(n, R)$ classical communication code over $\mathcal{N}$ consists of an encoding map $E: \{1,\dots,\lfloor 2^{nR}\rfloor\} \to \mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_A^{\otimes n})$ taking values in density operators, and a POVM decoding $\{D_m\}$ on $\mathcal{H}_B^{\otimes n}$; the maximal error probability is $p_e = \max_m\bigl(1 - \operatorname{Tr}[D_m\,\mathcal{N}^{\otimes n}(E(m))]\bigr)$. The classical capacity $C(\mathcal{N})$ is the supremum of rates $R$ for which there exist codes with $p_e \to 0$ as $n\to\infty$. Analogously, the quantum capacity $Q(\mathcal{N})$ is the supremum of rates $R$ at which $\lfloor 2^{nR}\rfloor$-dimensional quantum states can be transmitted through $\mathcal{N}^{\otimes n}$ with fidelity tending to $1$.

Known characterizations are regularized (multi-letter): 
$$C(\mathcal{N}) = \lim_{n\to\infty} \tfrac{1}{n}\,\chi(\mathcal{N}^{\otimes n}), \qquad Q(\mathcal{N}) = \lim_{n\to\infty} \tfrac{1}{n}\,I_c(\mathcal{N}^{\otimes n}),$$
where $\chi(\mathcal{M}) = \max_{\{p_i,\rho_i\}}\bigl[S(\mathcal{M}(\sum_i p_i\rho_i)) - \sum_i p_i S(\mathcal{M}(\rho_i))\bigr]$ is the Holevo information and $I_c(\mathcal{M}) = \max_\rho [S(\mathcal{M}(\rho)) - S((\mathcal{M}\otimes\mathrm{id})(|\psi_\rho\rangle\langle\psi_\rho|))]$ is the maximum coherent information. Both quantities are known to be superadditive on certain channels, so these limits do not in general reduce to their $n=1$ values.

Problem: Provide a single-letter (computable, non-regularized) formula, in terms of entropic or other quantities evaluated on a single use of $\mathcal{N}$, that equals the capacity of an arbitrary quantum channel $\mathcal{N}$ for transmitting (classical or quantum) information.
artifact.status_search_result: Current literature confirms there is no known single-letter formula for either the classical or the quantum capacity of a general quantum channel. The best general expressions remain regularized (multi-letter), and the phenomena of superadditivity and superactivation of coherent information demonstrate that such regularization cannot be removed by current techniques. Recent work (2024–2026) continues to investigate additivity in special channel families, and undecidability results suggest that a fully general computable formula may be unattainable.

status_evidence.title: Additivity of classical capacity and related problems – Open Quantum Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Each of these capacities is expressed through a regularized formula (multi-letter expression). There is still no complete characterization of the circumstances under which additivity holds.
status_evidence.claim: General quantum channel capacities are characterized only via regularized formulas; additivity fails in general.

status_evidence.title: On the undecidability of quantum channel capacities
status_evidence.snippet: Undecidability results for quantum channel capacities.
status_evidence.claim: There are undecidability barriers to obtaining a general computable capacity formula.

status_evidence.title: Super-additivity of quantum capacity in simple channels
status_evidence.snippet: Superadditivity of coherent information persists even in simple channel families.
status_evidence.claim: Superadditivity prevents reduction of regularized quantum capacity to a single-letter formula.
